column1: # @PLN140 phase 0 — what each instrument MUST say about a program whose hot spot is
# known in advance.  Written before the instruments existed; `make profile-corpus`
# checks it.  A row that stops holding is a regression in the PROFILER, not in the
# program.  Rationale, and what this corpus cannot prove:
#   doc/claude/PROFILE_ORACLE.md
# 06_newton_sqrt carries no `line` column on purpose: its two hot lines sit at 50.1 % and
# 47.9 %, too close to pin a winner run to run.  (It could not run under --interpret at all
# until loft#859 — the reassignment it was refused for now discharges at the division.)
# The `line` cells and 02's function follow the bench SOURCES, and those moved once: the
# @PLN158 harness gave every program a header comment and wrapped its kernel in a function
# (`fib` line 3 → 9, `main` → `mix` line 12, the two vectors lines 5|6 → 44|45), and the
# rows read stale for four days because nothing runs this oracle but a hand.  A bench edit
# re-pins its row in the same commit.
# frontend_large is the ENGINE row (@PLN166 A3): a compile of bench/frontend's large corpus,
# perf over loft's own Rust, read off `profile.sh --engine`'s BY-MODULE table — the module
# `data` (definition lookups, `def_nr` and its siblings) is the top module of every compile
# measured, 32–34 % over three runs against the allocator's 20–21 %.  The program is
# generated by `bench/frontend/frontend.py --emit large`, never committed.
# program        instrument  expect (regex, matched against the top-ranked row)  min_share  line
